quizzes.title: Reformed Multilateralism: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The 81st United Nations General Assembly opened on 8 September 2026 in New York, under the theme "Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All." On its sidelines, India's External Affairs Minister co-chaired the inaugural Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity (P4M) Summit with European Council President Antonio Costa. The P4M framework is built on the middle-power solidarity idea that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney set out at Davos. It was conceived in response to the erosion of global consensus, trade weaponisation and escalating conflicts across Europe and West Asia. Leaders of the European Union, Brazil, Kenya and Canada conceptualised the initiative, and India, Australia and Barbados co-sponsored it. It is designed as an open and flexible framework rather than another exclusive bloc or permanent bureaucracy. Its aims include strengthening international law, peace, multilateral cooperation and prosperity. It also seeks to enable countries from different political traditions to cooperate on reforming multilateral institutions and on common global challenges. At the same sidelines, India's External Affairs Minister took part in the 1st V4 plus India Foreign Ministers' Meeting, held during the Assembly week. India's position on reformed multilateralism was presented within this wider setting. The booklet presents the summit as one of the main events of the Assembly week.

questions.q: According to India, disruptions involving Fuel, Food, Fertiliser and Finance have a disproportionate impact on which group?
options: Developing countries and the Global South
Permanent members of the UN Security Council
questions.explanation: India said these disruptions hit developing countries and the Global South disproportionately.

questions.q: What did India call for to build more resilient global supply chains?
questions.explanation: India called for de-risking and diversification to make global supply chains more resilient.

questions.q: Through which groupings has India consistently pursued UN Security Council reform?
questions.explanation: The text says India has pursued UNSC reform through groupings such as the G4 and L.69.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Existing multilateral institutions are under pressure.
Reason (R): Geopolitical fragmentation and intensifying strategic competition are placing these institutions under pressure.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: India argued that geopolitical fragmentation and strategic competition are putting existing institutions under pressure.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Strategic chokepoints   ->   C. Greater representation of developing countries
II. Emerging technologies   ->   A. A source of supply-chain risk
III. Global institutions   ->   D. Comprehensive reform
IV. UN Security Council   ->   B. Guardrails sought by India
questions.explanation: Strategic chokepoints are a supply-chain risk, guardrails cover emerging technologies, representation is sought for global institutions, and comprehensive reform applies to the UN Security Council.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India called for greater transparency in global institutions.
II. India called for more inclusive decision-making in global institutions.
III. India argued that the 4F disruptions mainly harm developed economies.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: India called for transparency and inclusive decision-making, but the text says 4F disruptions hit developing countries disproportionately, not developed economies.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. India called for international frameworks and guardrails for AI, space security and digital technologies.
II. India called for building supply chains around a single country's production.
III. India pursues UNSC reform through the BRICS grouping.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since II contradicts the call for diversification and III names the wrong groupings.

quizzes.title: Visegrad Group: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Visegrad Group, usually called the V4, is a grouping that cooperates across several policy areas. Its members took part in a V4 plus India Foreign Ministers' Meeting held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York. The Assembly opened on 8 September 2026 under the theme "Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All." During the same sidelines, India's External Affairs Minister co-chaired the inaugural Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity Summit with European Council President Antonio Costa. The P4M framework is built on the middle-power solidarity idea that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney set out at Davos. It was conceived in response to erosion of global consensus, trade weaponisation and escalating conflicts across Europe and West Asia. It is designed as an open and flexible framework rather than an exclusive bloc or a permanent bureaucracy. India's position on reformed multilateralism was also set out during this period. The booklet places these developments within its September 2026 coverage of summits, reports and indices. The V4 meeting is one of the engagements India held with groupings during the Assembly week. It was held alongside the other meetings described in this part of the booklet. The Assembly's theme stresses trust and delivery for all.

questions.q: Which of the following areas is covered by the V4's cooperation?
questions.explanation: The text lists defence and security among the V4's areas of cooperation.

questions.q: In which year was the V4 established?
questions.explanation: The V4 was established in 1991, following the end of the Cold War.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a member of the V4?
questions.explanation: The four members are the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia, so Austria is not a member.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): All four V4 members belong to both the European Union and NATO.
Reason (R): The V4 grouping has four member countries.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the number of members does not explain their EU and NATO membership.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Name source of the group   ->   D. European Union and NATO
II. Members of the group   ->   C. Economic cooperation, energy and culture
III. Organisations shared by all four members   ->   A. A town in Hungary
IV. Economic and cultural areas of cooperation   ->   B. Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia
questions.explanation: The group is named after a town in Hungary, its members are the four Central European countries, all four belong to the EU and NATO, and the economic and cultural areas are listed as cooperation areas.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The V4's cooperation covers energy and culture.
II. The V4's cooperation excludes defence and security.
III. The V4 is named after a town in Poland.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since defence and security is a listed cooperation area and the name comes from a town in Hungary.

How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The V4's cooperation covers political and diplomatic coordination.
II. The V4 was established before the end of the Cold War.
III. All four V4 members belong to the EU but not to NATO.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the V4 was established after the Cold War and all four members belong to both the EU and NATO.

quizzes.title: Arctic Council: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Arctic has moved up the international agenda as melting ice opens new maritime corridors, including the Transpolar Sea Route. Control and influence over Arctic sea lanes are expected to shape future global trade and naval power projection. China describes itself as a near-Arctic state and is investing in Arctic research and infrastructure, while Russia has heavily militarised its Arctic coastline. The United States views Greenland as central to countering both. Greenland, the world's largest island, lies between North America and Europe, which gives it a strategic position for monitoring naval movements in the North Atlantic. Pituffik Space Base, formerly known as Thule Air Base, is a US facility for monitoring potential missile threats from Russia, China and North Korea. Denmark's firm stance highlights the tension between territorial sovereignty and the strategic ambitions of major powers. Within this wider competition, the Arctic Council is a platform through which countries discuss the region. Its members are the countries whose territory lies inside the Arctic area, and countries from outside the region also take part in its work. The Council gives these countries a place to talk through issues affecting the Arctic. Its discussions are reported in the booklet's coverage of Arctic affairs. Its members are not the only states with an interest in the region.

questions.q: Through which declaration was the Arctic Council established in 1996?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Council was established in 1996 through the Ottawa Declaration.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a member nation of the Arctic Council?
questions.explanation: Japan is not among the member nations listed in the text.

questions.q: How often does the Arctic Council's chairmanship alternate?
questions.explanation: The text states that chairmanship alternates every 2 years.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Arctic Council was established in 1996.
Reason (R): It provides a forum for discussion and cooperation on the Arctic environment and sustainable development.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the Council's purpose does not explain the year of its establishment.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Chair of the Council in 1996-1998   ->   B. Climate change and its impact on the Arctic region
II. India's status in the Council   ->   A. Inter-governmental platform
III. Main focus of the Council   ->   D. Canada
IV. Type of body   ->   C. Observer since 2013
questions.explanation: Canada chaired the Council in 1996-1998, India has been an observer since 2013, the main focus is climate change, and the Council is an inter-governmental platform.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Arctic Council is an inter-governmental platform.
II. Greenland is one of the member nations of the Arctic Council.
III. India has been an observer of the Arctic Council since 2008.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the member nations are the eight listed countries and India has been an observer since 2013.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Russia is one of the member nations of the Arctic Council.
II. The main focus of the Council is maritime trade routes.
III. The Arctic Council was established in 1996 through the Ottawa Declaration.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II wrongly names maritime trade routes as the main focus.

quizzes.title: Arctic Council: Typed Answer
quizzes.passage: The Arctic has moved up the international agenda as melting ice opens new maritime corridors, including the Transpolar Sea Route. These routes could reduce travel time between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, lower fuel and shipping costs, and bypass the Panama and Suez canals. Great powers are competing for influence in the region, and China describes itself as a near-Arctic state. Russia has heavily militarised its Arctic coastline, while the United States regards Greenland as central to countering both. Greenland lies between North America and Europe, a position that makes it significant for monitoring naval movements in the North Atlantic. Pituffik Space Base, formerly known as Thule Air Base, is a US facility for monitoring potential missile threats from Russia, China and North Korea. Denmark's firm stance highlights the tension between territorial sovereignty and the strategic ambitions of major powers. The Arctic Council is a forum through which countries discuss the region's environment and development. Its members are the countries whose territory lies inside the Arctic area, and countries from outside the region also take part in its work. Denmark has indicated that the arrangement could support a sustained NATO role in Greenland and the wider Arctic. The Council also has a secretariat, which the booklet mentions in its coverage of the body.

questions.q: In which year was the Arctic Council established? (year)
questions.explanation: The Arctic Council was established in 1996 through the Ottawa Declaration.

questions.q: Through which declaration was the Arctic Council established? (one word)
questions.explanation: The Arctic Council was established in 1996 through the Ottawa Declaration.

questions.q: How often, in years, does the Arctic Council's chairmanship alternate? (number)
questions.explanation: The chairmanship of the Arctic Council alternates every 2 years.

questions.q: In which year did India become an observer of the Arctic Council? (year)
questions.explanation: India has been an observer since 2013.

questions.q: Which country chaired the Arctic Council from 1996 to 1998? (one word)
questions.explanation: Canada was the first chair, for 1996 to 1998.

questions.q: What is the Arctic Council's main focus? (two words)
questions.explanation: The main focus of the Arctic Council is climate change and its impact on the Arctic region.

questions.q: What kind of platform is the Arctic Council? (one word, hyphenated form accepted)
questions.explanation: The Arctic Council is an inter-governmental platform.
